subject.title: Backend loopback client loses operator scope when the relay forwards from the host's own interface IP (agent RPC fails: missing scope: operator.write)

question: Should internal gateway backend calls migrate to process-bound authority before shared-token scope preservation is removed, or should host-interface peer addresses intentionally qualify as local-equivalent shared-auth clients?
rationale: The reported workflow needs the existing scope-preservation path, while the canonical security issue seeks to remove that path; selecting the permanent authority model is an explicit Gateway/secops decision.

options.title: Migrate backend authority first
options.body: Give internal backend calls a dedicated runtime credential or device-token path, prove agent and approval workflows, then remove the shared-token bypass.

options.title: Extend same-host locality
options.body: Accept host interface peer addresses only for backend shared-auth locality, with fail-closed interface discovery and explicit remote-denial coverage.

options.title: Keep strict loopback only
options.body: Declare interface-forwarded self-calls unsupported and add diagnostics, accepting that affected installations must reconfigure their relay.

recommendation.title: Migrate backend authority first
recommendation.body: Give internal backend calls a dedicated runtime credential or device-token path, prove agent and approval workflows, then remove the shared-token bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently changed the exact local shared-auth and device-identity behavior and are best positioned to reconcile the caller with the hardening direction.
